draft.title: Australian environmental law
card: The Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999 (Cth), called the EPBC Act, is the Commonwealth's main environmental law. It was passed by the federal Parliament.

The Act protects matters of national environmental significance. These include world heritage properties, wetlands of international importance, listed threatened species and ecological communities, and listed migratory species.
A person who wants to take an action that is likely to have a significant impact on one of these matters must apply for approval from the federal Environment Minister.

The Act is not a ban on all development. It sets out a process for assessing impacts, and approval can be refused or given with conditions. Most other environmental matters are mainly dealt with by state and territory laws.
draft.remember: The EPBC Act is the federal law that requires approval for actions likely to significantly affect matters of national environmental significance.

a.q: Which of these is protected under the EPBC Act as a matter of national environmental significance?
opts: A listed threatened species
A local council's street trees
A private backyard garden
A suburban park's playground
a.why: The Act covers matters of national environmental significance, and listed threatened species are one of them. Street trees, gardens and playgrounds are local matters, so they are not covered by the Act unless they also affect a protected matter.
a.clue: Think of matters that matter to the whole nation, not one street.

b.q: A company plans a mine likely to significantly affect a listed threatened species. Under the EPBC Act, what must it do before it starts?
opts: Apply for approval from the federal Environment Minister
Wait until the species is removed from the threatened list
Seek a permit only from the local council
Prove the mine will have no effect on any living thing
b.why: An action likely to have a significant impact on a protected matter needs federal approval, and the Minister can refuse it or add conditions. The Act does not ban all development, so the company does not need to show there is no effect at all.
b.clue: The Act sets up an approval process, not a total ban.

b.best: Apply for approval from the federal Environment Minister

problems.detail: The three wrong options (a backyard garden, street trees, a playground) are obviously local and trivial. With the clue, a Year 12 student can pick the answer without knowing the list of matters of national environmental significance. Plausible distractors, such as a state-listed local heritage building or an ordinary local creek, would test the idea better.

a.q: Which of these is protected under the EPBC Act as a matter of national environmental significance?

A wetland protected only by a state law
A building on a state heritage register
A creek that flows through one country town

a.clue: Is it on the national list, or only a state or local one?
